transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

It is actually quite normal for plastic tubs to remain wet in a Bosch Serie 4. Plastics do not retain heat well during the wash, so they don't get hot enough for the condensation drying process (where steam from other dishes dries everything else) to work effectively on them. However, if your glasses and china are also coming out with water droplets or feeling cold, that suggests a drying issue rather than just normal plastic behaviour. The most common fix is to top up the rinse aid, which helps water sheet off surfaces. Could you check if the rinse aid reservoir is full? Also, please let me know if the glassware is warm at the end of the cycle.
The rinse aid is empty, the symbol is lit on the display. I use all-in-one tablets though. The glasses have some droplets but they're not cold, it's steamy inside at the end.

Since the glasses are warm and steamy but wet, this suggests a drying issue rather than a heating fault. The empty rinse aid is probably the main culprit; rinse aid makes water sheet off dishes instead of forming droplets that cling to surfaces. All-in-one tablets often contain less rinse aid than needed for optimal drying in Bosch machines. Please top up the rinse aid reservoir and ensure the dispenser setting isn't on the lowest level. Also, check which programme you used: Eco or Quick cycles often skip the heated dry phase to save energy, leaving items wet. Try a standard 65°C cycle with the rinse aid topped up and see if that resolves it.
I use Eco 50 every time, and I open the door straight away when it finishes. I'm happy to try the rinse aid and a different programme though. Where do I find the dispenser setting?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. On Bosch Serie 4 models, the rinse aid dispenser is located inside the door, next to where you put your detergent. Open the door and look for a blue cap with a water drop symbol on it. Twist this cap counter-clockwise to unscrew it; underneath is a dial that controls how much rinse aid is released. Turn this dial so the arrow points to a higher number (such as 3, 4, or even 6) rather than the lowest setting (0 or 1). This ensures enough rinse aid is used to help water sheet off your glasses and plates. Once you've adjusted it, screw the cap back on tightly.
Ok, I've found the cap and I'll turn the dial up. Does it matter that I use all-in-one tablets, or should I still fill the rinse aid with the liquid stuff?

Yes, you should still fill it with liquid rinse aid. All-in-one tablets contain a fixed amount of rinse aid that is often not enough for Bosch dishwashers to dry effectively, especially on Eco cycles which use lower temperatures. By topping up the reservoir and setting the dial higher (e.g., 4 or 6), you ensure there is enough chemical agent to make water sheet off your dishes rather than cling as droplets. Try this with a standard cycle next time; if items are still wet, we can look at whether the Eco programme itself is skipping the drying phase.
Ok, I'll fill it with liquid rinse aid and set the dial higher, then try a different programme. I'm not sure if mine has an extra dry option though, is that something I should look for?

Yes, most Bosch Serie 4 models do have an 'Extra Dry' option. It is typically a button on the control panel, often marked with a snowflake symbol or the words 'Extra Dry', rather than being part of the programme selection itself. You usually press this before starting the cycle to enable additional heating during the drying phase. Since you are currently using Eco 50, which prioritises energy saving over heat, enabling Extra Dry (if available) or switching to a hotter programme like Intensive 70 will significantly improve drying results.
Ok, I'll have a look at the control panel for an extra dry button. I'm not sure if mine has one though. Anything else I should do once I've tried it?

The most important thing to do is test it properly. Switch from Eco 50 to a hotter programme like 'Normal 65°C' or 'Intensive 70°C', as these use higher temperatures that help water evaporate and dry effectively. Run this with the newly topped-up rinse aid, but leave the door closed for about an hour after the cycle finishes to let the condensation drying process work its magic before opening it. If the dishes come out dry afterwards, the issue was simply the programme choice; if they are still wet despite the hotter wash and fresh rinse aid, we will need to look at other factors like spray arm blockages or the filter.
